answer: Each live key may lease only one uplink slot on a mesa-top repeater whose licenses are hard-capped and non-transferable mid-epoch. Enrollment records the slot's delay profile through a vine of independent listeners while a zephyr-driven anemometer feed is mixed into the challenge nonce. To stay enrolled, the agent must answer a random probe from that exact slot; listeners reject any second key on the same license or a mismatched delay profile. A farm therefore has to buy and site a new radio and license for every alias, a linear capital and logistics cost that software forking cannot share.
